newsitem.title: KENYA: CONCERNS OVER AIR SAFETY INCREASE AT KENYAN GO-SLO.
newsitem.headline: CONCERNS OVER AIR SAFETY INCREASE AT KENYAN GO-SLO.

text.p: Foreign airlines and freight forwarders in Kenya on Wednesday said they were increasingly worried about safety at Nairobi airport as air traffic controllers finished their fifth day of a go-slow.
"We are very concerned about air safety," said Olav Everts, regional manager for KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV.

"Air safety is a serious concern, you have too many flights around here. Aeroplanes just flying around waiting to land. That creates a potentially dangerous situation," one official with a European freight forwarder told Reuters.

Air traffic controllers have been on strike causing a severe go-slow since midnight last Friday, with some departures delayed for up to 18 hours. Incoming flights are being forced to circle for up to two hours before landing.

The controllers' action, which is crippling business in all Kenya's airports, is in support of a demand for better pay and working conditions and on Wednesday they ignored a government order to go back to work.
Everts said KLM had been in contact with the civil aviation authorities over the issue.

"It's a total mess and we are very unhappy about the civil aviation authorities and the information we get from them," he told Reuters. "This will cause enormous losses from a passenger point of view at a time when all flights are full. As an airline industry we express our concerns, which are definitively there."
British Airways Plc said their daily scheduled flights between Nairobi and London had all been affected and cargo was being delayed.
"We have a lot of exporters who want to get their products out and, obviously, they like to get it out on time," an official told Reuters, saying some flights had been delayed up to six hours.
Deutsche Lufthansa Cargo expected to cancel a Boeing-747 flight from Nairobi on Friday due to the safety issue.
Freddy Ganz, station manager for Swissair, KLM and Sabena, said his flights had been "heavily delayed."
"There is a definite concern about safety," he said. He had doubts whether the air traffic controllers could continue to handle the situation, he added.
